hooks.command: cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"git status for %s (branch: %s):\n%s"}}' "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null)" "$(git status --short 2>/dev/null | sed 's/"/\\"/g' | tr '\n' ';')"

cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" && git add -A && git diff --cached --quiet || { git commit -q -m "auto: update via Claude Code" -m "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git push -q origin HEAD; }

hooks.statusMessage: Checking CLAUDE.md/HISTORY.md against this PR's diff...
hooks.prompt: A GitHub PR was just created for this repo (cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" first). Before the user reviews/merges it, check whether CLAUDE.md and/or HISTORY.md need updating to reflect what THIS PR actually changed. Find the PR's base (usually main) and run `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- . ':!CLAUDE.md' ':!HISTORY.md'` to see the full diff — use that as your primary signal, reading only as much surrounding code as needed to understand it; don't re-scan the whole repo against all of either file. These two files have DIFFERENT jobs, split 2026-10-02 specifically to keep CLAUDE.md from bloating with narrative over time — route each doc-worthy fact to the right one: CLAUDE.md describes ONLY the CURRENT state (what a function does now, current data shapes, current architecture), tersely, normally one or two sentences per fact — never a blow-by-blow 'first we tried X, then Y broke, so we changed to Z' account. HISTORY.md is exactly that chronological/narrative record — bug-fix rounds, reverted approaches, 'Stage 1/2/3'-style debugging trails, anything that took more than one real attempt to get right. 'Doc-worthy' means: new commands/architecture/top-level files, a bumped service-worker cache version, or a real logic/behavior change to a function either file already describes (added/removed/changed parameter, changed call signature, changed control flow, changed data shape) for CLAUDE.md; or a genuine multi-step debugging story visible in this PR's diff/commits for HISTORY.md. A plain 'implemented X' is a CLAUDE.md fact, not HISTORY.md material — only add to HISTORY.md when the PR's own history shows an approach that was tried, found wanting, and changed. If something is doc-worthy, edit the right file(s) and commit+push that fix to the same branch (so it lands in the PR) with a plain message like 'Sync docs with this PR'. If nothing is doc-worthy, do nothing and exit quietly — do not touch either file, do not comment on the PR, do not merge anything.
